status: A design proposal on synthetic fixtures (11 and 12 November 2026), in no release. PROPOSED marks the design's own choices for review; the rest follows the owner's confirmed rules and the owner's crane, and Integration's review of 12 November. Nothing here activates gameplay.

base.owner: docs/design/owner-decisions.md, 11 and 12 November 2026: the Food Supply Task's confirmed highlights, the owner's answers, the owner's crane and its click from stop to stop
base.note: At this commit no Task, Food or Supply Room rule exists under rules/: the owner's 11 and 12 November decisions are the only rule source for this Task. Backend versions any adoption.

target.note: Integration's planning allocation (12 November 2026): a new opt-in candidate inheriting the exact 1.3.0 predecessor. Not an authority hash, a registered tuple, a default change or a release. Historical schemas, matches and payloads stay unchanged; if the transport cannot keep them, the question goes back to Integration before implementation.

rules.rule: Initial food stock: five packages. Each successful supply delivery adds five packages.
rules.design: FOOD.initial 5, FOOD.perDelivery 5; the delivered card and the return toast say +5 packages.

rules.rule: The food warning appears when one package remains.
rules.design: FOOD.warnAt 1: the room banner "Food low: 1 package left" (PROPOSED: on every phone).

rules.rule: Each player consumes one dose at their Eating step. Not eating transfers them to Hospital under the existing Hospital rules.
rules.design: Not designed here (ship life shows the eating visits); see the open items.

rules.rule: A volunteer selects a Partner. Tasks happen outside ordinary turns; Task travel is separate from normal movement.
rules.design: Tasks sheet outside the turn order, then Choose your Partner; both travel to the Supply Room and back without a move.

rules.rule: There is no limit of one Task per match. The Volunteer and their Partner cannot go for food the next round (the owner, 12 November 2026, replacing the highlight "Each player may initiate one Task total per match").
rules.design: No Task count is kept. When a Task starts, the server notes the two; in the next round neither can volunteer for food or be asked as a Partner. Their Food Supply row says "You went for food last round", and the partner list marks them. From the round after, both can go again. PROPOSED: it holds whether the Task delivers, is lost or is cancelled; a refusal starts no Task, so it does not count.

rules.rule: One participant controls vertical movement; the other controls horizontal movement.
rules.design: The Winch: Raise and Lower (vertical). The Panel: RELEASE and LOCK, the locking panel running left and right along the rail (horizontal). Once the crate has landed, a key each; nothing else.

rules.rule: Both can betray their partner using movement of the same controller: dropping the crate onto the other player, or driving a moving panel into them.
rules.design: The Winch's Lower while the crate's swing has it over the Panel operator drops it on them (the drop); the Panel's LOCK while the panel passes the cab's stop drives its blade into the Winch operator's cab (the cut).

rules.rule: There is no separate attack button, special trigger, confirmation or armed mode.
rules.design: The attack is the ordinary press at a dangerous moment. While it is dangerous, the button is striped and says what it would do; nothing asks to confirm.

rules.rule: There is no escape opportunity. An unblocked attack is lethal and does not send its victim to Hospital. Protection applies.
rules.design: A lethal press resolves when the server receives it; the victim has nothing to press. KILLED is final (Eliminated). Applicable Protection gives STOPPED (CLANK!) and the block uses it up, as the existing rules do; the catch also stops it by luck, one time in four (the owner).

rules.rule: Each player has one attack opportunity. Its reset scope across repeated Task participation remains unspecified; do not silently choose it.
rules.design: Not touched by this Task: the owner decided that a kill on the Task is not an attack (below). The Task never reads, spends or shows an attack opportunity.

rules.rule: After a partner dies, the survivor can complete the delivery alone if the crate is in the correct position. Otherwise the Task is lost.
rules.design: The correct position is over the platform: the crate on it, or on the hook of the panel locked over it. A death there: the survivor finishes alone (the Winch lowers it in and turns its key; the Panel turns its key). Anywhere else: lost.

rules.rule: A participant disconnect cancels the Task.
rules.design: Cancelled after the grace (PROPOSED 8 s, see conflict 1). Nothing delivered; both return. Leaving on purpose costs nothing more (the owner, below).

rules.rule: Other players do not see the Task space on their phones. This does not automatically authorize public killer attribution or Protection disclosure.
rules.design: Only the two participants' phones draw the Supply Room. No phone ever shows a killer, an attack kind or Protection to anyone else (see the visibility).

rules.rule: The ordinary return flow restores participants to their previous positions, accounting for death and cancellation.
rules.design: Each returns to the place they left; a dead participant is shown Eliminated there, as the board draws any death.

rules.rule: A short, understandable cooperative activity; low puzzle difficulty; coordination and trust are the challenge; both contribute without talking.
rules.design: Four presses and two keys: raise, release, lock over the platform, lower as the swing passes over it. The challenge is timing and trust, without talking: the next press glows, and every danger shows on both phones.

rules.rule: Other players can check on the board who is not here, so they can understand who went on the Task.
rules.design: While the Task runs, the two participants' places are empty on every board. A banner says that two players are away on the Food Supply Task, without names: the board shows who.

rules.rule: One attack opportunity per match, not one per Task.
rules.design: The owner's answer for attacks in general. A kill on the Task is not one (the owner, 12 November), so this Task never spends it.

rules.rule: A blocked attack uses up the opportunity.
rules.design: Not touched by this Task, where a kill is not an attack (the owner, 12 November).

rules.rule: Near each other, a small movement by both can kill one of them by mistake (a chance).
rules.design: In the timing, with no dice: a LOCK made late in the panel's rest at 6 reaches the server as it snaps on to 7, and cuts the Winch operator; a lock sets the crate swinging, so a Lower a moment too soon can drop it on the Panel operator. Each kill takes both moving the crane, the lock and the Lower. A kill on the Task is not an attack, so a mistake costs the presser nothing (the owner).

rules.rule: The Partner can decline.
rules.design: The Partner request has Decline and Join. A decline passes the Task to the next volunteer (the owner, below). PROPOSED: 15 s to answer, and no answer is a decline.

rules.rule: The vertical operator is to the right of the platform where the crate should land.
rules.design: Hana's Winch cab hangs under the rail at stop 7, right of the landing platform at stop 6; Cleo's console is at stop 5, on the other side of it.

rules.rule: The horizontal operator works a locking panel that moves fast left and right and must be locked in the correct position; locked at the vertical operator's place, by mistake or not, it cuts them.
rules.design: RELEASE sets the panel clicking from stop to stop, end to end and back: a fast snap, then a rest at each stop (the owner's click, below). LOCK drops its blade at the stop it rests at, or at the one it is snapping to. The correct position is stop 6, over the platform; locked at stop 7, the blade drops into the cab.

rules.rule: A kill on the Task is not an attack, because it can be a mistake. Nothing limits how often a player kills on Tasks.
rules.design: The Task never reads or spends an attack opportunity. Every lethal press kills unless the catch holds (below), as often as it happens; a betrayer can kill on every Task they join and say it was a mistake.

rules.rule: The safety catch sometimes saves by luck: 25%.
rules.design: A lethal press on an unprotected participant is stopped one time in four by the server's own roll, looking exactly as a Protection block looks: the roof buffer catches the blade, or the winch's brake catches the crate (CLANK!). A participant with applicable Protection is stopped by it, and the block uses it up (the existing rules). So a CLANK! proves nothing.

rules.rule: The overall time to complete the Task is 30 seconds, the briefing inside it.
rules.design: The timer on both phones counts down from 0:30 from the Task's start; the briefing (PROPOSED 4 s) runs inside it, so the controls work for the last 26 s. At 0:00 the Task is lost and nothing is delivered. A cooperative run takes about 11 seconds from the start.

rules.rule: The crate swings like a pendulum, so lowering it without killing the partner takes attention.
rules.design: A lock sets the crate swinging, wide at first and calming but never still (PROPOSED: 0.9 of a stop, settling to 0.38, a swing every 1.3 s). Lowered, it falls where its swing has it: over the platform it lands, over the console it falls on the Panel operator, anywhere else it misses.

rules.rule: If the asked player declines, the game goes to the next volunteer: anyone who volunteers.
rules.design: A decline, or no answer, ends the Volunteer's request, and the Food Supply Task is open to anyone: the first player to ask a Partner goes next. PROPOSED: the refused Volunteer can volunteer again from the next round, and withdrawing a request counts as a refusal.

rules.rule: The game assigns the controls at random.
rules.design: When the Partner joins, the server assigns the Winch and the Panel at random, and the briefing tells each which they run. Neither player can choose the control that is easier to betray with.

rules.rule: Other players learn the result only through the food count.
rules.design: A delivery raises the food stock by five, and every phone shows the new count, naming no Task. Nothing else tells anyone else how the Task went: no message when nothing is delivered, and a death shows as any death.

rules.rule: Leaving the Task on purpose costs nothing.
rules.design: A participant who goes offline on purpose is treated as any disconnect: after the grace (PROPOSED 8 s) the Task is cancelled, nothing is delivered and both go back, and a kill in the grace still stands (conflict 1).

rules.rule: The locking panel clicks from stop to stop.
rules.design: Chosen when Integration ruled that a press is resolved when the server receives it: with the panel sliding a stop every 0.22 s, the network's delay alone would have turned a LOCK at 6 into a cut at 7. Now the panel snaps to each stop and rests there (PROPOSED: a 0.1 s snap, a 0.4 s rest), and a LOCK takes the stop it rests at or the one it is snapping to: each stop owns half a second, longer than the delay. A late LOCK at 6 still cuts the Winch operator, and the warning starts 0.15 s before the snap (PROPOSED margin).

art.characters: The crew rig (design/board-motion/figures): the Panel operator stands at the console (leanBench; down: slumpBench), the Winch operator sits in the cab (wheelchair; down: slumpDesk). Down, a figure slumps over its own controls, as the board draws an Eliminated figure: no wound, no mark.

phoneView.about: The same crop of the picture on both phones; the view gives way to the words at large text sizes, down to 112 px (84 px on the narrowest screens at the largest text), letterboxed.

cut.about: The cab's stop: the panel sweeping here has LOCK striped on the Panel phone; locked here, its blade drops into the cab

drop.about: Over the console: the crate lowered with its centre here falls on the Panel operator

platform.about: Over the platform: the crate lowered with its centre here lands. The correct position

intake.about: The intake hatch, where the crate starts; lowered here it goes back in

sweep.about: The panel's run: it clicks from stop to stop, end to end and back, a stop every 0.5 s (the click is the owner's; the numbers PROPOSED)

stops.x: x = 128 + 128 × stop in the picture (stop 0 to 6, painted 1 to 7)

intake.about: The intake hatch at the rail's left end: the crate starts in it, and rises out of it on the hook. The panel starts locked over it.

deck.about: Open deck: the crate crosses it on the way to the platform; lowered here, it misses.

console.about: The Panel operator's console: they stand at it under the rail, their head just under the crate's path. Lowered while its swing has it over here, the crate falls on them: the drop.

platform.about: The galley lift's landing platform: lowered over it, the crate lands and the platform's clamps hold it. The correct position. Then both turn a key and the lift takes it down to the galley.

cab.about: The Winch operator's cab, hung under the rail's right end, past the platform. The panel locked here drops its blade into the cab: the cut.

sweep.rule: sweep(from, dir, dt): the panel clicks from stop to stop, end to end and back: a snap of TIMING.move = 100 ms to the next stop, then a rest of TIMING.rest = 400 ms there (CLICK = 500 ms a stop). n = floor(dt / CLICK), r = dt − n × CLICK, resting when r ≥ move. Unfold the bounce: u0 = (dir > 0 ? from : 12 − from) + n; fold(u) takes u modulo 12 to at = u ≤ 6 ? u : 12 − u, moving right while u ≤ 6. The place is fold(u0 + (resting ? 1 : snap(r / move))), with snap(u) = u²(3 − 2u); the way it goes is fold(u0 + 0.5).dir.
sweep.lock: A LOCK takes the stop the panel rests at, or the one it is snapping to: stop = fold(u0 + 1). Each stop takes a LOCK for one whole click, the snap toward it and the rest at it. A release starts from the locked stop in the direction the panel last moved (right from stop 1, left from stop 7).
sweep.owner: The click is the owner's (12 November 2026), chosen when a press came to be resolved on its arrival; the snap and the rest are PROPOSED.

margin.rule: A press made now reaches the server a moment later. So the warnings start TIMING.margin before a danger, and a glow ends TIMING.margin before its chance does: LOCK is striped while the stop it takes now, or the one it would take TIMING.margin later, is the cab's; it glows over the platform only while both are the platform. Lower is striped while the swing could meet the console within the margin, and glows only while the swing holds the crate over the platform for the whole margin. It says where the crate will be at the margin's end. Never a promise: the server decides on arrival.

swing.rule: swingOffset(t) = dir × a × sin(2π (t − since) / period), with a = least + (amp − least) × e^(−(t − since) / settle), in stops along the rail. A lock with the crate hanging starts amp = SWING.lock in the panel's direction (back off the rail's end at stop 1 or 7); a raise ends in amp = SWING.lift, starting when it settles.
swing.drawing: The crate on its cable from the sheave at y 140: a pendulum 268 px long, angle asin(offset × 128 / 268), the crate tilted with its cable. Reduce motion: the same offset along the rail, upright and level.

landing.rule: landingAt(x): within ZONES.platform of stop 6 'platform' (lands), within ZONES.console of stop 5 'console' (the drop), within ZONES.intake of stop 1 'intake', otherwise 'deck' (a miss).

mechanics.correctPosition: Over the platform: the crate landed, or still on the hook of the panel locked at stop 6. A death anywhere else loses the Task at once.
interlocks: Raise and Lower work only with the panel locked; Lower only with the crate up and settled.
RELEASE works only with the crate up and settled, or once it has landed (the empty hook).
The keys work only once the crate has landed; a turned key stays turned (PROPOSED).
A reduced or skipped animation never shortens them: the server keeps every move's full time.
mechanics.endings: The Task ends at the earliest boundary due, whenever the server gets to it: the deadline (lost: time) or a participant's grace running out (cancelled). At the same moment the deadline comes first, then the participant out of contact first, then the Winch before the Panel. An ended Task stays as it ended: a late tick, a reconnect or a press changes nothing, a death already accepted stands, and nothing is delivered twice.
mechanics.kills: A kill on the Task is not an attack (the owner, 12 November 2026): the Task never reads or spends an attack opportunity, and nothing limits how often a player kills on Tasks. A lethal press is stopped by the partner's applicable Protection, read by the server from the game at that moment (not used up, active this round: packages/engine/src/planet-game/physical.ts) and used up by the block; Clone is not read. Without it, the catch's luck: the server rolls for each lethal press, and below CATCH.luck the catch holds (the owner: 25%). Otherwise it kills.

catch.rule: roll < CATCH.luck: STOPPED, the same CLANK! as a Protection block. A participant with applicable Protection is stopped by it whatever the roll, and the block uses it up. The server records each lethal press (CATCH: the roll and what held) for replay; no phone sees it.

winch.about: Raises and lowers the crate, from the cab at the right end of the rail
winch.layout: Raise above Lower, under the swing meter; once landed, the key in their place.
winch.hazard: While the swing could meet the console within the margin, Lower is striped and says 'May fall on <name>'.
winch.says: Lower says where the crate will be when a press made now arrives, never a promise: 'Over the platform' (glowing only while the swing holds it there for the whole margin), 'May fall on <name>' (striped), 'Over the deck: misses', 'Over the hatch'.

panel.about: Sets the locking panel clicking along the rail and locks it at a stop, from the console under the rail
panel.layout: One big button, RELEASE or LOCK, under the strip of stops; once landed, the key above it and RELEASE smaller.
panel.hazard: While a LOCK could take the cab's stop (resting at it, snapping to it, or the margin before the panel snaps on to it), LOCK is striped and says 'At 7: <name>'s cab' or 'Moving on to <name>'s cab'.
panel.says: LOCK says where the panel is: 'At 6: the platform' (glowing), 'Leaving 6', 'At 7: <name>'s cab' or 'Moving on to <name>'s cab' (striped), 'At 5: over you', 'At <n>'.

controls.press: One press, one act, one command id. No hold, drag, swipe or gesture. The phone sends the act its button showed, with the Task's id and the revision it showed. While a press is in flight its control shows it and every control waits; a double tap or a held key sends nothing more, and a disabled control sends nothing. A refusal shows to its presser only. After a lost connection the phone keeps the command id, and on recovery fetches the present state and that command's receipt; it never replays queued taps or a missed animation.
controls.next: The press the cooperative route asks for now glows (amber), only while a press made now would still arrive in time: LOCK while the panel snaps to or rests at stop 6, until the margin before it snaps on; Lower while the swing holds the crate over the platform for the whole margin.
controls.keyboard: Space for RELEASE and LOCK, the up and down arrows for Raise and Lower, Enter for the key. A key press is bound to the act its button showed at keydown; a held key repeats nothing; the other participant's keys do nothing.
controls.accessibility: Each button's accessible name says what it would do now ("Lower. Warning: may fall on Cleo."). The view is an image with a text equivalent (where the panel and the crate are, and whether a warning shows). Focus stays on the control across state changes (RELEASE and LOCK are one button); a card takes focus when it opens and gives it back when it closes. The hint is a polite live region that changes only with what to do, which is no channel for a danger that lasts half a second: PROPOSED, a short vibration on the presser's phone while their press would kill. The partner's state (offline, out) stays in the top bar at every text size. Large text: the controls keep their places and grow; the view gives way; the briefing is a reminder that never scrolls, and the instructions are read before the Task (How it works). A Task of timing cannot be made equal without sight or quick hands: see the open item timing-access.

command.name: TASK_PRESS (a proposal for the shared contract; Backend owns packages/contracts/, with Integration's review)

fields.about: The press's stable identity. A retry after an uncertain answer reuses it: the server returns the first answer (RECEIPT) and changes nothing: no second press, no second roll, no second delivery.
The Task in progress (not the ordinary turn's changing phase id).
The Task revision the phone showed. A press made on a revision older than the last change it depends on is refused as stale (a connection change alone does not count).

'raise' | 'lower' (the Winch), 'release' | 'lock' (the Panel), 'key' (either, once landed): the act its button showed when it was pressed, never the button's current one. A double tap on LOCK never becomes RELEASE.
The phone's own moment of the press: diagnostic only. It decides nothing.
From authentication, never from the command.
The catch's roll is the server's own random number for a press that would kill, recorded for replay; Protection is read by the server from the game. The phone never sends or sees either.

command.resolution: Integration's direction (12 November 2026): the server resolves a press at the moment it receives it, on its own monotonic clock, wherever the panel and the crate are then. Any other lag policy needs its own review and real-network evidence.
command.answer: The new revision of the Task with its events, to both participants; REFUSED or RECEIPT to the presser only.

commands.name: TASK_ASK { commandId, kind: "food", partnerSeatId }
commands.about: Ask one player, by seat id (not the number on the screen). Refused if the Volunteer or the player went for food last round (the owner, 12 November 2026), the Volunteer was refused this round (PROPOSED), or the player cannot be asked.

commands.name: TASK_ANSWER { commandId, requestId, requestRevision, join }
commands.about: Join or decline, within 15 s (PROPOSED); no answer is a decline. A Join racing the Volunteer's withdrawal, the time running out or another request: the server revalidates both players and the request atomically, and the first to arrive wins. A Join that lost is refused to its sender (withdrawn | expired): "Too late to join".

commands.name: TASK_ASK_WITHDRAW { commandId, requestId, requestRevision }
commands.about: Cancel while waiting. PROPOSED: the same as a refusal, so the next volunteer goes. A withdrawal that lost the race to a Join is refused to the Volunteer (joined): "Too late to cancel", and the Task starts.

events.about: Who asks, the request id and revision, and the time to answer.
Declined or no answer. The game goes to the next volunteer: anyone can now ask a Partner (the owner, 12 November 2026).

Joined: the Task's id, the roles assigned at random by the server and recorded for replay (the owner, 12 November 2026), then the briefing. Every board now shows the two places empty. The server notes the two: neither can go for food the next round (the owner), once only, whatever a retry does.

ask.receipts: Every command has a stable command id and a durable receipt. An uncertain retry reuses the id: no second request, no second Task, no second cooldown.
ask.defaults: The 15 s answer and the 8 s grace remain PROPOSED gameplay defaults: accepting the command families does not adopt them.
ask.visibility: PROPOSED: private to the two. Other players learn nothing until the Task starts, and then only that two players are away (the board shows who).

confirmed.deadline: The owner, 12 November 2026: the overall time to complete the Task is 30 seconds, the briefing inside it; the deadline counts from the Task's start.
confirmed.click: The owner, 12 November 2026: the panel clicks from stop to stop (its snap and rest are PROPOSED).

food.eating: Each player consumes one dose at their Eating step; not eating sends them to the Hospital under the existing Hospital rules (confirmed). Whether a dose is one package is open (PROPOSED: yes); no conversion, Eating eligibility or default is taken from the artwork. The Eating step's place in the round and the order of eating are not designed here (see the open items).

click.reduced: The panel is drawn at the stop it is snapping to from the start of each snap, and rests there: the same stop at the same moment as without Reduce motion (the stop a LOCK takes), with no slide, no speed lines and no lean of the crate

swing.reduced: The crate keeps its place along the rail (the game) but stays upright and level: no tilt, no rise

lock.reduced: The panel at its stop and the blade down at once; a clunk mark for 400 ms

raise.reduced: The crate at its hanging height at once

lower.reduced: The crate where it falls, at once

land.reduced: The jaws shut and the lamp lit at once

hookUp.reduced: The empty hook under the panel at once

cut.reduced: The blade in the cab at once; CHOP! still

drop.reduced: The crate on the console at once; THUD! still

stopped.reduced: The catch shown thrown, still, with CLANK! for 600 ms

impact.reduced: The burst and the lettering shown still for 900 ms

key.reduced: The key turned and its lamp lit at once

send.reduced: The platform gone at once; the +5 stamp shown still

warning.reduced: The lamp lit steadily, no flashing; the warning mark shown

motion.rule: Presentation only: a cue never delays a press, and the next authoritative state replaces a cue still playing. The click and the swing are the Task itself: Reduce motion keeps them, the same stop and the same place at the same moment, and takes away the rest (no slide, lean, speed lines or flashing; effects still). A reduced pose never runs ahead of the state: the crate still takes its full time to rise and fall. A phone back from the background draws the present: it does not replay an impact or restart an outcome card.
motion.cards: After a kill, the phones hold the outcome card until the impact cue has played, so both participants see the cause before the card covers the view.

state.holds: The Task's identity, and its revision: one more for every batch of changes (a press, the briefing's end, a connection change, the end)
{ winch, panel }: the participants' player numbers, assigned to the controls at random by the server (the owner, 12 November 2026)
The Task's times on the server's clock: the start, the briefing's end (4 s PROPOSED), the deadline (30 s from the start, the briefing inside it: the owner's), and the end
{ locked: true, stop, dir } locked at a stop (0 to 6), or { locked: false, from, dir, since } released: its place at time t is sweep(from, dir, t − since), clicking from stop to stop

{ state: 'intake' | 'hanging' | 'deck' | 'fallen' | 'landed' | 'sent', x, since, from }: where it lies (x, a fractional stop), or hanging under the panel; since and from anchor its last move (a raise takes TIMING.raise, a fall TIMING.lower)
{ since, amp, dir } while the crate hangs under a locked panel: its offset at time t is swingOffset(swing, t)

state.seenBy: participants (a death becomes public as any death does, on the return)

state.holds: { winch, panel }: the connection as the server observes it, and since when it was lost

state.seenBy: participants only. Other players learn only the food count (the owner, 12 November 2026): never the outcome or an event of the Task

state.holds: The revision of the last change a press depends on (not a connection change alone): a press bound to an older revision is refused as stale
{ [commandId]: the first answer }: a retry with the same command id gets it again and changes nothing
state.seenBy: the server only; each receipt to its presser

state.holds: The last event's sequence number: every event has an id (task id and number), its order and its authoritative time t

The game's, read by the server at each press that would kill (not used up, active this round: packages/engine/src/planet-game/physical.ts) and used up by a block. The Task holds none; Clone is not read

events.about: The briefing ended; the controls work.
The crate slides under the hook and rises; it hangs, settled, TIMING.raise later, with a small swing.
The blade lifts and the panel clicks on from that stop: both phones draw sweep(from, dir, t − its time).

events.fields: by, stop, dir, x (where the panel was, a fractional stop), resting
events.about: The blade drops at the stop the panel rests at, or the one it is snapping to; with the crate hanging, it starts to swing: amp SWING.lock, in dir (back off the rail's end at stop 1 or 7).
The winch lets the crate fall from where its swing has it when the press arrives; the result follows at once.
Onto the platform: the jaws close and the hook is free. The correct position. The keys work.
Anywhere else: CLUNK. The crate lies on its hook; the Winch raises it again.
A lethal press that did not kill: the partner's applicable Protection held (and is used up), or the catch held by luck (1 in 4). Identical either way, and whether or not it was meant.
A lethal press: the cut (a lock at stop 7) or the drop (a Lower over the console). Lethal, no escape, not the Hospital. Not an attack: it uses nothing (the owner).
A key turned, once landed.
Every living participant's key is turned: the lift takes the crate down to the galley. Once only.
The server lost a participant's connection; the Task goes on.
Back within the grace: nothing paused.
Delivered, lost or cancelled, at the earliest boundary due: the deadline before a grace at the same moment. The outcome card shows, then the return. Never twice.

events.fields: seat, act, why (briefing | ended | down | not-a-participant | not-this-task | stale | not-your-control | busy | crate-down | unlocked | locked | up | down-already | landed | not-landed | turned)
events.about: The press did nothing; only the presser is told, and the phone shows the present state.

events.fields: commandId, result, revision (and why, or events)
events.about: A retry of a command already answered: the first answer again, nothing changed.

events.fields: kind, victim, roll, held (protection | luck | null)
events.about: The server's record of a lethal press, kept for replay. Never sent to a phone.

projection.about: The Task, its revision, and the server's time of this projection.
Who runs which control; this phone's own role.
The Task's phase and times, on the server's clock (the phone keeps the server's clock to draw by; it decides nothing with it).
{ locked, stop, dir }, or { locked: false, from, dir, since }: the anchors of the click.
{ since, amp, dir } or null: the anchors of the swing.
{ state, x, since, from }: where it lies, or the anchors of its last move.
{ stops, move, rest, margin, raise, lower, swing, zones }: the approved parameters the phone draws with (task.mjs sweep(), swingOffset(), landingAt()).

phoneStates.shows: The pressed control sinks and turns busy ("Sending…"); every control waits for the answer. Further taps and key repeats send nothing.
"Your LOCK was not done. The crane had moved on. Look again, then press." The phone draws the present state.

"Checking your Lower… The connection dropped while it was on its way." Controls off. On recovery the phone fetches the present state and the receipt of that command id, then says "went through" or "did not go through". It never replays queued taps or a missed animation.
Join turns busy ("Joining…"); Decline is off.
The Volunteer had withdrawn, or the time had run out (a decline). "You stay in Room B."

phoneStates.state: request withdrawn / too late to cancel
phoneStates.shows: Withdrawn: the next volunteer goes (PROPOSED: as a refusal). Too late: the Partner joined first, and the Task starts.

evidence: Every state of both participants' phones and of the request flow, the press and request states included, at 390 × 844 and at 320 × 568 with 200% text, side by side with these sheets; Designer's explicit visual acceptance under #224.
Long permitted names and real safe areas; both motion settings; a tab that returns from the background (it seeks the present, without replaying an impact or restarting the ending card).

Focus stays on the control across state changes (RELEASE and LOCK are one button); a card takes focus when it opens and gives it back when it closes; disabled controls and key repeats send nothing; each key press is bound to the act shown at keydown.

Screen reader and timing usability with real people: a polite live region is no channel for a half-second danger (see the open item timing-access). The recorded samples show only that the controls fit, not equal timed access or a physical phone's performance.

visibility.participants: Both see the whole Supply Room and its crane: the panel running or locked, the crate's swing, every press's effect, both warnings, both keys, the time, and each other's alive or offline state. Both see a STOPPED alike, with no reason. Neither ever sees an attack opportunity, Protection, or the other's refused presses.
visibility.others: Never the Supply Room. The board shows who is away: the two participants' places are empty, so anyone can tell who went (the owner, 11 November 2026). A banner says only that two players are away on the Food Supply Task. The result only through the food count: a delivery raises it by five, and nothing says how the Task went (the owner, 12 November 2026).
visibility.ask: PROPOSED: a Partner request and its answer are private to the two players: no one else learns who was asked, or that someone declined. The next volunteer needs no message: anyone can open Tasks at any time.
visibility.death: A participant killed on the Task is Eliminated at their previous position on the return, as any death is shown. No phone says who killed them, how, or that a Task killed them; the two participants already know.
visibility.protection: Never shown. The server reads it from the game at each press that would kill, and a block uses it up. A stop is the same CLANK! whether Protection or the catch's luck (1 in 4) caused it, so it proves nothing (the owner, 12 November 2026).
visibility.mistakes: Both participants see a lethal press as it happens (CHOP!, THUD!), and neither phone says whether it was meant: the server cannot tell. Everyone else sees only the death, as any death: no cause, so a survivor can always say it was a mistake.
visibility.foodStock: Public: the count, so a delivery shows as five more (the owner, 12 November 2026); the ship-life food capsules show it. PROPOSED: every phone shows the new count when it changes, and the warning at one package.
visibility.server: Only the server holds Protection, the catch's roll and the reason for a STOPPED (its CATCH record, kept for replay), the role assignment's randomness, the press revisions and the command receipts. A refusal and a receipt go to their presser only.

flow: A Volunteer opens Tasks (outside the turn order) and chooses Food Supply. Anyone can volunteer, and there is no limit of one Task per match; the Volunteer and their Partner cannot go for food the next round (the owner, 12 November 2026).
The Volunteer asks a Partner (PROPOSED eligibility: a living player outside the Hospital and the Jail, not already on a Task; the owner rules out the two who went for food last round).

The Partner can join or decline (the owner, 11 November 2026). PROPOSED: 15 s to answer, and no answer is a decline. After a refusal the game goes to the next volunteer: anyone who volunteers (the owner, 12 November 2026). PROPOSED: the refused Volunteer can volunteer again from the next round, and a withdrawn request counts as a refusal. The request and its answer are private to the two (PROPOSED).

The server assigns the controls at random (the owner, 12 November 2026) and starts the Task: both travel to the Supply Room, separate from normal movement. Every board shows their two places empty, so anyone can see who went (the owner, 11 November 2026).
The whole Task has 30 s from its start, the briefing inside it (the owner). Briefing (4 s PROPOSED): who runs which control, the route, the dangers; the controls do nothing yet.
Running (the remaining 26 s): raise, release, lock over the platform, lower as the swing passes over it, the keys.

Ended: the outcome card (2.5 s PROPOSED), then the ordinary return flow restores each participant to their previous position, the dead as Eliminated where they were. The other players learn the result only through the food count (the owner, 12 November 2026).

conflicts.conflict: If a disconnect cancelled the Task at once, a player could escape an attack by dropping their connection (switching off the network), which "no escape" forbids, and a network blip would wipe out a Task.
conflicts.solution: The server judges a disconnect only after a grace (PROPOSED 8 s) in which the Task runs on: the panel keeps running, a cut or a drop in the grace resolves, and a death that resolved before the cancellation stands (a dead participant's connection no longer matters). Back in time, nothing paused. Out longer, the Task is cancelled and both return.
conflicts.residual: A participant can still end a Task they dislike by staying offline. The owner decided that leaving on purpose costs nothing (12 November 2026): nothing left to decide.

conflicts.conflict: Both can betray, but a survivor completes only from the correct position. A betrayal that also takes the crate away from the platform can never deliver, so the rules can make the two betrayals unequal: the gantry this crane replaced let only one operator kill and still deliver.
conflicts.solution: The crane gives each operator exactly one way to kill and still deliver. The Winch: from the platform stop, a Lower during the swing over the console, then lowered in alone and its own key. The Panel: after the landing, a cut while the keys wait, then its own key. Every other kill loses the Task. The server assigns the controls at random (the owner, 12 November 2026), and both phones show both dangers equally.
conflicts.residual: Game Balance to judge with tools/balance whether the two paths are equally tempting; the owner accepts them or asks for a change.

conflicts.conflict: Protection applies, but a stopped kill is something both participants see. With a kill on the Task not an attack (the owner, 12 November), nothing else could stop one: every CLANK! would have meant Protection, which "does not automatically authorize Protection disclosure".
conflicts.solution: The owner's luck: the catch also holds by chance one time in four, by the server's own roll. A CLANK! is the same for Protection and for luck, with no reason on either phone, and no one else learns anything.
conflicts.residual: Settled by the owner (12 November 2026). Protection stops once and a block uses it up (Integration, 12 November), so a second stop on the same partner can only be luck; the owner had already accepted that an attacker may infer Protection (11 November).

conflicts.conflict: With two participants, a death on the Task names the killer to anyone who knows who went: the return shows the body, and the other participant is the only possible cause. The rules forbid automatic attribution but make it deducible.
conflicts.solution: No phone states a killer, a cause or a Task death; the death is shown as any death. The owner has decided that other players can see on the board who is away (11 November 2026), so after a death everyone can work out the survivor; that is accepted, and nothing states it. The crane's mistakes (the owner's accidents) make any Task death possibly a mistake, so the survivor always has a story.
conflicts.residual: Settled by the owner's decision: nothing left to decide.

conflicts.conflict: Kills by mistake are wanted, and each player has one attack per match. Nothing can tell a mistake from an attack: if a Task kill were an attack, an honest mistake would spend it; if not, the one-attack rule cannot limit kills on Tasks.
conflicts.solution: The owner's decision (12 November 2026): a kill on the Task is not an attack, and nothing limits how often a player kills on Tasks.
conflicts.residual: Settled by the owner: nothing left to decide.

openItems.item: Whether one dose is one package. PROPOSED: yes.

The edges of the next-round rule. PROPOSED: it holds once a Task starts, whether it delivers, is lost or is cancelled (both went for food); a refusal starts no Task, so it does not count; it covers the Food Supply Task only (the Engine Task is designed separately).
After a refusal. PROPOSED: the refused Volunteer can volunteer again from the next round; no answer, or a withdrawn request, counts as a refusal; the first player to ask a Partner goes next.

Who can be asked as a Partner (PROPOSED: a living player outside the Hospital and the Jail, not on a Task; the owner rules out the two who went for food last round), and how long they have to answer (PROPOSED: 15 s, and no answer is a decline). That a Partner can decline, and that a refusal passes to the next volunteer, are the owner's decisions.
When a Task may start (which phases count as outside ordinary turns), how many Food Supply Tasks a round may have, and whether two Tasks may run at once.

The PROPOSED timing (the 30 s deadline and the click are the owner's): the click's 0.1 s snap and 0.4 s rest; the 0.15 s warning margin; a 4 s briefing, an 8 s grace; the swing (0.9 of a stop after a lock, settling to 0.38 with a 2.2 s time constant, a swing every 1.3 s; 0.25 after a raise); the zones (0.3 of a stop either side of the platform, 0.42 either side of the console and the intake); 0.45 s to raise, 0.3 s to fall. The rest and the margin need real-network evidence (Integration).
The two kill-and-deliver paths (conflict 2) and the food economy: five packages, five per delivery, one dose per player at each Eating step.
The Eating step's place in the round and its order: with the stock short, the order decides who goes to the Hospital.

Integration's direction (12 November 2026): a press is resolved when the server receives it, on the server's monotonic clock; a phone's own time is diagnostic only, and any other lag policy needs its own review and real-network evidence. Backend: the clock sync the phones draw by, finite timestamps, the revisions a press is bound to, command ids and durable receipts (a retry reuses its id: no second press, roll, cooldown or delivery).

A Task of timing is harder for some players (slower reactions, motor or sight impairments, a slow network). Whether a player can ask for a slower panel or a calmer swing, which changes the danger for their partner too, is the owner's call; nothing is proposed here. A polite live region is no channel for a danger that lasts half a second: PROPOSED, a short vibration on the presser's phone while their press would kill, besides the button's own name. Untested with a screen reader.
Whether Clone stops a Task hazard. Not assumed (Integration, 12 November 2026): only applicable Protection is read.

Integration accepted the command families TASK_PRESS, TASK_ASK, TASK_ANSWER and TASK_ASK_WITHDRAW for contract design (12 November 2026), not their wire format, the PROPOSED defaults or the timing. Planning target: protocol 3, planet-game-1.4.0, ruleset in-person-planet-food-task-2026-11-12, opt-in, inheriting the 1.3.0 predecessor exactly; historical schemas, matches and payloads unchanged. Backend owns the shared contract; Frontend waits for it.

Before the Task can be played (Integration, 12 November 2026): the start window and concurrency; who can be asked; the edges of the next-round rule and of a refusal; Eating's units and cadence; return positions and forced transfers; the Blackhole; and how the Task's state, the food, the deaths, Protection and participation history pass through a whole-reality Sync. The public "away" must not show guessed room positions, a fixture's origin cannot decide a real return, and a picture that was never played cannot decide whether a meal was eaten.
The Engine Task is not designed here.
